subject: Media Literacy
title: The 24-Hour News Cycle
description: A micro-lesson that makes The 24-Hour News Cycle usable.

hook.text: CNN launched in 1980 with 24-hour news. By 2000, the need to fill airtime had permanently changed journalism.

buildup.text: The 24-hour news cycle demands constant content, pushing outlets to cover stories before facts are confirmed.

discovery.text: Empty airtime gets filled with speculation, opinion panels, and repeated coverage of dramatic but minor stories.

twist.text: Speed replaced accuracy as the competitive advantage. Being first matters more than being right.

climax.text: The news cycle creates artificial urgency. Not everything needs to be 'BREAKING' just because airtime needs filling.

punchline.text: 24 hours of news doesn't mean 24 hours of things worth reporting.

quiz.question: How did the 24-hour news cycle change journalism?
options: It improved accuracy by allowing more time for research
Speed replaced accuracy as the competitive advantage
It had no effect on news quality
